title: mockOS live-provider divergence ledger
status: Seeded from source review; no live capture has run yet
notes: Every difference a live parity run finds must resolve to an entry here.
An unledgered difference is reported as a defect.
intentional=false means the difference is a known bug that is tracked but not yet fixed; it still reports as a defect.
field is a dotted path into the normalised observation. A trailing * matches any deeper path.

entries.reason: The software TOTP factor accepts only the static synthetic passcode 000000. RFC 6238 time steps, drift, enrollment, and shared secrets are not implemented.
Tokens issued after the factor and session bridge keep acr urn:okta:loa:1fa:any. mockOS does not model MFA assurance elevation.
The ID token always carries amr [pwd] regardless of the factor path taken.
Tenant identifiers are derived deterministically from the environment seed so runs are reproducible. A real tenant id is assigned by the provider.
UserInfo is deliberately omitted from discovery until an executable route exists, rather than advertised and unimplemented.
UserInfo is deliberately omitted from discovery until an executable route exists.
The Entra device policy omits verification_uri_complete by design; Okta includes it.
Group overage emits a claim source at 201 groups with a 1000-id fallback ceiling. Real Entra thresholds and endpoints differ.
Error descriptions, trace and correlation identifiers, and timestamp formatting are synthesised. The OAuth error code is the comparable field, not the prose.
Okta error summaries and errorId values are synthesised; errorCode is the comparable field.
mockOS emits a token_use claim on Entra tokens. Real Entra v2 tokens have no such claim. Not yet fixed.
The Entra access token uses client_id as its audience and carries the full ID-token claim set. Real Entra scopes the audience to the resource API. Not yet fixed.
Discovery advertises pairwise subject types while sub equals oid equals the user id, which is public, not pairwise. Not yet fixed.
Discovery advertises query-only response modes while the HTTP adapter accepts and implements form_post. Not yet fixed.
The Okta access token uses client_id as its audience. A real custom authorization server uses its own audience, typically api://default. Not yet fixed.
The Okta groups claim carries display names while Entra carries identifiers. Both are deliberate and provider-shaped.
The authorize endpoint requires openid in scope. Real Entra permits resource-only scopes, so a resource-only authorize request diverges. Not yet fixed.
Discovery constants cloud_instance_name and tenant_region_scope are fixed synthetic values.
Rate-limit headers are fixed synthetic constants rather than a real quota.
Hosted login is mockOS-branded with no session cookie, so every authorize re-prompts. prompt, max_age, acr_values, and domain_hint are ignored.
A non-numeric passCode is rejected at the HTTP layer with E0000001 before the factor comparison, where real Okta returns E0000068. Not yet fixed.
Revocation returns 200 with a null body and no content-type.
Entra emits the string "2.0" and Okta the number 1. Both are deliberate and provider-shaped; assert the exact type.
The device user code is eight characters from a custom alphabet, matching neither provider's real format.
The Entra error timestamp renders ISO 8601 with the T replaced by a space and the Z retained.
